text: Delete the elements from the argument list numbers in place and return that same (mutated) list.
The sentence is cut short and means 'that occur more than once': every value that appears two or more times in numbers is removed entirely (all of its copies); values that appear exactly once remain.

Contradiction with R-RM-3: the restrictive clause 'that occur' presupposes that only some elements are removed and the others are kept, which requires a selecting condition the sentence does not state.
The sentence is cut short and means 'that occur more than once': every value that appears exactly once in numbers is kept; values that appear two or more times are not kept at all.

Contradiction with R-RM-1: the restrictive clause 'that occur' presupposes that only some elements are removed and the others are kept, which requires a selecting condition the sentence does not state.
The prompt states no order for the result: the remaining elements may be returned in any order.
